rule: Automated reviewer identity is single-sourced in the reviewer-identity.jq module and every consumer routes through it
description: The automated-reviewer registry (which products are automated reviewers, their logins, and their approval-signal kind) and the identity predicates over it (`strip_bot`, `is_self`, `reviewer_matches_filter`, `reviewer_is_approver`) live in exactly one place: plugin/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/reviewer-identity.jq. Consumers reach it two ways: the jq filters fix-history-classify.jq and the two jq programs inside pr-change-detect-poll.sh carry `include "reviewer-identity";`, and every shell call site that runs fix-history-classify.jq passes the module search path with `jq -L <dir holding the module>` (prefilter.sh directly; fetch-normalize.sh through _shared/fetch-normalize-core.sh, which derives that dir from the classifier path). The identity predicates gate on the author's account type, so every GraphQL selection whose rows reach a type-gated predicate requests `author { login __typename }`. This fixture owns three axes. (1) CANONICAL CLAIM. The source pin sits on the registry declaration `def automated_reviewers:` in reviewer-identity.jq: deleting or renaming the registry turns the suite red. The registry entries themselves are deliberately unpinned so adding or editing a reviewer product does not break the suite; registry content is proved by the behaviour suites, not here. The self predicate is pinned on `def is_self($login; $type; $self): $type == "User"` in reviewer-identity.jq, a span that carries both the definition name and its account-type gate, so deleting or renaming `is_self` or dropping the `User` type gate (reverting self identity to a login-only compare) turns the suite red. (2) CONSUMER WIRING. pr-change-detect-poll.sh is pinned twice, once per jq program, on a span covering the `-L "$SCRIPT_DIR"` invocation AND the `include "reviewer-identity";` that opens the program body, so dropping either the search path or the include at either call site stops the match. prefilter.sh is pinned on its classifier invocation `jq -r -L "$SCRIPT_DIR" -f "$CLASSIFY_FILTER"`. _shared/fetch-normalize-core.sh is pinned on its classifier invocation `jq -c -L "$classify_module_dir" -f "$classify_filter_path"` and on the derivation that binds that dir to the classifier's own directory, so pointing `-L` anywhere else fails. The query literals are pinned per selection on spans that include the neighbouring field list (`nodes { author { login __typename } body url reactionGroups` and so on), because the bare substring `author { login __typename }` also appears in header comments of fetch-normalize.sh and would survive the query losing `__typename`. The poll's comment and review-thread selections feed the type-keyed self predicate `is_self`, so they are pinned too, on spans that include the parent connection (`comments(last: 50) { totalCount nodes { databaseId author { login __typename } } }` and `comments(last: 1) { nodes { databaseId author { login __typename } } }`), because the bare node selection `nodes { databaseId author { login __typename } }` occurs in both and a bare pin would survive either one losing `__typename`. These query pins are the ONLY guard on query drift: the behaviour tests inject payloads and bypass the live GraphQL queries entirely, so a query that stopped requesting `__typename` would make every type-gated predicate silently reject every author while the tests stay green. (3) INCLUDE IS LIVE CODE, AND NO SECOND COPY. set_check extracts, from lines whose first non-blank token is the literal (comment lines begin with `#` and never match), either `include "reviewer-identity";` or a definition of one of the module's six names (`def automated_reviewers`, `def approval_kinds`, `def strip_bot`, `def is_self`, `def reviewer_matches_filter`, `def reviewer_is_approver`). fix-history-classify.jq and pr-change-detect-poll.sh are checked in `equal` mode against the single-member set {include}: this proves the include sits on a real code line (fix-history-classify.jq also names the include inside a header comment, so a plain presence pin there would survive deleting the live include), and any redefinition of a module name in those files is an extra and fails. prefilter.sh, fetch-normalize.sh, and _shared/fetch-normalize-core.sh are checked in `subset` mode against the same set, so a module name redefined inside any of their embedded jq programs fails. The capture group is a fixed literal alternation rather than a negated-delimiter class because the axis is presence of one known literal plus absence of known definition literals, not membership of an enumerable marker set: a broad `def [a-z_]+` capture would also see each consumer's own legitimate helper definitions. RESIDUALS, stated plainly: these pins claim word-sequence presence in the named files, never meaning, and never that the code executes. A NEW consumer file not named here is invisible: a new script that queries review authors without `__typename`, invokes the classifier without `-L`, or re-declares the registry is not caught (set_check `files` is a literal list with no glob expansion). A rewrite that keeps every pinned substring while bypassing the module — for example matching inline login literals in a consumer that still includes the module — is not caught by this fixture; the closure test in tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh covers reintroduction of registry login literals. A second copy of the registry under a different name, or one whose `def` is wrapped so the name does not follow `def ` on the same line, is invisible to the set_check because extraction is line-scoped and case-sensitive. The `is_self` pin proves the definition's word sequence is present, not that any consumer calls it: a consumer that drops its `is_self` call in favour of a login-only compare keeps this fixture green. The self-compare closure check in tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh covers login-only self compares in the consumer files it names; a NEW consumer file is invisible to it as well.
